findings.title: DiskPressure: the kubelet is evicting pods (13.7% free)
findings.evidence: root filesystem (nodefs): 12.8 GiB free of 93.2 GiB (13.7%). The kubelet evicts pods below 5% (nodefs.available<5%) and then keeps evicting until 15% free (14.0 GiB) (minimum reclaim 10%). Container images are on the same filesystem. DiskPressure is True since 2026-09-27 23:32 UTC.
findings.meaning: The disk that holds container logs, emptyDir volumes and writable layers (and on k3s also the images) is close to the kubelet's hard eviction threshold.
findings.why: At the threshold the kubelet sets DiskPressure, evicts pods (BestEffort first) and deletes unused images, and it does not stop at the threshold: it frees until 15% free (14.0 GiB).
findings.fix: Eviction continues until 15% free (14.0 GiB): free at least 1.2 GiB now to get above 15% free. Do not prune images yet: 2 pods use images that exist only on this node (imagePullPolicy: Never): sre-lab-app/url-shortener-6f89bdc657-jxxl8, sre-lab-app/url-shortener-6f89bdc657-vktnd. Push them to a registry or save them first (k3s ctr images export), and remove only named images. In this order: (1) what is outside Kubernetes: build caches (go clean -cache, docker builder prune) and old logs (journalctl --vacuum-size=500M); (2) named images you know a registry still has (crictl images, then crictl rmi <image>); (3) only then crictl rmi --prune, which deletes every image that no running container uses, including the images of evicted, crash-looping or scaled-down workloads.
findings.verify:
df -h /   # above 15% free
kubectl describe node k8server | grep DiskPressure   # False

findings.title: 2840 pods were evicted
findings.evidence: Stopped by the kubelet (DisruptionTarget TerminationByKubelet, or reason Evicted): argocd/argocd-server-7d9f-abcde and 2839 more.
findings.meaning: The kubelet stopped these pods to protect the node (disk, memory or PID pressure). Their records stay until deleted.
findings.why: Evictions mean the node ran out of something; the records also hide the real pods in lists.
findings.fix: Find what ran out, fix that, then delete only these records by name: kubectl delete pod -n argocd argocd-server-7d9f-abcde … (2839 more). Do not delete by phase across all namespaces: that also removes failed Job pods kept for debugging.
findings.verify: kubectl get pod -n argocd argocd-server-7d9f-abcde   # NotFound
